newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunfire ends Pakistan opposition march.
newsitem.headline: Gunfire ends Pakistan opposition march.

text.p: Gunfire and tear gas ended a big opposition march in the Pakistani city of Lahore on Monday after protesters hurled stones at the Punjab provincial assembly building, witnesses said.
Authorities said four people, including two policemen, were injured in the clash that they said was started by the protesters who, in turn, blamed the police.
Up to 40,000 people joined the march staged by 14 opposition parties campaigning to force Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto to step down to make way for mid-term elections, witnesses said.
After stoning the assembly building, demonstrators ransacked the office of the assembly's security officer, witnesses said.
They said police first fired teargas canisters and then shots in the air to disperse the crowd.
But a government statement later said the shots were fired by the protesters and that the police fired tear gas after the crowd became uncontrollable.
"Today it is the verdict of the people of Lahore that Benazir should quit," opposition leader Nawaz Sharif earlier said in a speech to the marchers.
"Nothing is left for Benazir; she has completed her days," he said. "I warn her that she should herself give up power or this nation will make her go."

The march was the biggest anti-Bhutto demonstration since Sharif's mainstream Pakistan Muslim League (PML) and 13 other groups formed the "Pakistan Bachao" (save Pakistan) movement in August to campaign against the prime minister's three-year-old government, which they accuse of corruption.

Bhutto denies the charges and accuses opposition politicians of campaigning against her to escape prosecution for their own alleged wrongdoings committed when Sharif was prime minister for 32 months until July 1993.
"We will bring Nawaz Sharif and make Benazir run away", the demonstrators chanted as they marched about three km (two miles) from Lahore's Neela Gunbad marketplace to the assembly chambers.
"This nation is not ready to tolerate you any more," Sharif said of Bhutto. "In three years Benazir has ruined the country."
